Never reset or destructively rewrite the database; use additive migrations, explicit backfills, versioned records, feature flags, audit events and compensating actions.
Tourify, the federation and each member organization remain separate entities with separate authority, governance, finances and responsibilities.

No Tourify account, upload, Rights Passport, Phase 8 consent or Phase 9 cooperative membership implies federation membership, data transfer, voting delegation, representation, collective licensing or bargaining authority.
Default to local organization sovereignty; absence of an explicit delegation means no delegation.
No federation decision may modify a local creator membership, rights claim, licence, payment instruction, enforcement case or governing document.
Credentials are evidence statements and never expand the underlying source authority.

Every credential verification checks approved issuer, schema, proof, holder binding, jurisdiction, scope, issue time, expiry, suspension and revocation; high-risk actions also check the live source record.
Every mandate is exact-scoped, time-bound, revocable and prohibits subdelegation unless expressly approved.
No cross-entity data pooling or cross-border transfer occurs without new purpose-specific authority, lineage, transfer mechanism, localization review and onward-transfer controls.
External registries, regulators, courts, CMOs, standards bodies and government identity systems remain authoritative for their own records and decisions.
No coordinated price, rate, bid, refusal to deal, market allocation, collective licensing, bargaining or representation workflow ships without a separate legal and entity approval package.
All external submissions, credentials, mandates, votes, status updates, transfers and partner events are idempotent, versioned, attributable and auditable.
Key management, trust registry administration, finance and audit deletion cannot be controlled by one unreviewed administrator.
Stop work when authority, entity, membership, consent, transfer, jurisdiction, competition, privacy, security, standards profile, provider contract or required approval is unclear.
